analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift BASE excerpts and the complete patch. HEAD lines 705–716 add selected-model recovery state, a test load override, and saved/committed enabled-model snapshots; HEAD line 868 initializes the saved filter from configuration. These changes alone introduce no demonstrated authorization bypass, plaintext exposure, or unsafe resource allocation. Existing process-key generation, attestation signer selection, model eligibility filtering, slot limits, cache artifact identities and cancellation bookkeeping are unchanged in this file. The response-encryption comment at BASE lines 10–11 is not evidence of a changed encryption contract; the canonical coordinator remains a trusted plaintext hop.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery and its callers: whether recovery respects retirement/self-test exclusions (BASE 417–430), verified weight bindings (614–621, 764–779), fleet memory/load serialization (410–416, 564–576), and shutdown/drain or connection barriers (447–455, 482–488). Relevant threats include T-007/T-012/T-027 for recovered model integrity, T-010/T-029 for cancellation and residency availability, T-041 for cache binding, and T-053 for serving authorization during lifecycle transitions. Also reconcile savedEnabledModels and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch with policy refresh, committed switches and status publication so configuration observation does not accidentally change serving authority. Recovery implementation and changed callers are not supplied here; their contracts remain unverified, not observed missing controls. Deeper integration review is needed to resolve that material new recovery behavior.
